title: Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Authorization Amendment Act of 2026
summary: As introduced, the bill would establish a Commercial Autonomous Vehicles Program within the District Department of Transportation allowing certain autonomous vehicles to transport passengers and goods in the District. Applicants and permit recipients would have to submit planning documents, reports and data to DDOT.
takeaway: Would establish a Commercial Autonomous Vehicles Program within the District Department of Transportation allowing certain autonomous vehicles to transport passengers and goods in the District.

title: Autonomous Vehicle Requirements
summary: As introduced, the bill would require manufacturer documentation and Department of Transportation review of automated driving capabilities, allow the sale and registration of vehicles classified at Level 2 subject to annual owner reporting, and prohibit the sale or public-road automated operation of vehicles classified at Levels 3, 4, or 5.
takeaway: Would restrict higher-level automated driving systems in Illinois and introduce manufacturer review and owner reporting requirements.

title: Motor vehicles; oversight of commercial vehicle parking
summary: Act 464 amends Louisiana's autonomous commercial motor vehicle provisions (R.S. 32:400.2, 400.3 and 400.7) alongside a highway-shoulder parking change: the state gets sole and exclusive agency jurisdiction over autonomous commercial motor vehicles and automated driving systems, and the written pre-operation certification for driverless trucks and teleoperated trucks is filed with the Department of Public Safety and Corrections, office of state police, rather than DOTD.
takeaway: Act 464 shifts the certification filing for driverless and teleoperated commercial trucks to state police and gives the state sole jurisdiction over autonomous commercial vehicles and automated driving systems.

title: Autonomous vehicles; traffic violations
summary: Sets the process for citing traffic violations by autonomous vehicles: a POST-certified or state-commissioned officer must determine an offense occurred, notice goes by first-class mail to the registered owner within 20 business days with a Tennessee return address and 30 days to pay, and a second notice with another 30 days is required before added penalties. A Senate amendment defines automated driving system terms and lets state or local law enforcement adopt ADS enforcement policies consistent with the process. Enacted as Public Chapter 726.
takeaway: Creates a mailed-notice process for traffic citations issued to the owners of autonomous vehicles in Tennessee.

title: Implements of husbandry; autonomous; automated
summary: Amends A.R.S. 28-101 so the definition of 'implement of husbandry' covers agricultural implements or vehicles that use an automated driving system or are autonomous. Signed by the Governor March 31, 2025 as Laws 2025, Chapter 19.
takeaway: Extends Arizona's 'implement of husbandry' definition to autonomous and automated agricultural vehicles.

title: Driverless-capable vehicles transporting hazardous materials
summary: Amends Iowa Code 321.515(1) to bar operation of a driverless-capable vehicle carrying hazardous materials without a conventional human driver, as a simple misdemeanor. Renumbered from House study bill HSB 598. House Transportation recommended passage 20-0 on 2/18/2026; placed on the calendar under unfinished business on 3/19/2026 with no later floor action recorded.
takeaway: Would bar driverless-capable vehicles from carrying hazardous materials in Iowa without a human driver.
